Garden water

Deep Forensic All Paths Taken Analysis

The first model snapshot contains entries 1 through 16. The second keeps those entries and adds 17 through 36. Each snapshot records what the description contained at that point. Water movement at a particular site remains unmeasured.

Six questions to ask of the list

Branching · What leaves the puddle?

The first list gives three exits through soaking into soil, running downhill and evaporating. The second adds a drinking bird. The count of immediate puddle exits moves from three to four. Entry 4, entry 5, entry 6 and entry 21.

Return · Can water reach a bird again?

Droppings deliver water to soil. Roots take it up, the stem carries it to fruit, and a bird can eat that fruit. The route returns to a bird. Its identity and the number of completed trips are open. Entry 23, entry 7, entry 17, entry 19 and entry 20.

Convergence · What feeds the stream?

One route runs downhill and crosses the bank in entry 5 and entry 33. Another soaks into soil, seeps deeper and enters through the streambed in entry 4, entry 8, entry 31 and entry 32. Both can feed floodplain soil when the stream overflows in entry 34.

Boundary · What happens beyond the garden?

Evaporated puddle water can travel on the wind and condense on a neighboring roof. The gutter and barrel collect it. A hose can bring it back to garden soil. Entry 6, entry 16, entry 27, entry 28, entry 29 and entry 30.

Detail · When do two entries describe one transfer?

Plant water reaching fruit is the broad description in entry 12. Water moving from the stem into developing fruit in entry 19 specifies how that can happen. The same overlap occurs between new growth in entry 11 and a growing leaf in entry 18.

Unresolved connection · Which water is on the leaf?

Water arriving at a growing leaf is inside its tissue. Dripping and surface evaporation start with water outside. Dew supplies one possible external source. The record leaves open whether the water in the growing leaf ever reaches its surface as a liquid. Entry 18, entry 1, entry 2, entry 3 and entry 14.
